themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign hazards spiked dramatically THIS WEEK with 4 complaints vs. a baseline of 0.4 per week (967% increase, z-score 7.49), representing an emerging public safety concern that could endanger pedestrians and cyclists in Park Slope.
evidence: 4 dangling street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Classified as high-severity anomaly in 311 data
reporting_angles: Conduct visual inspection of major intersections (Prospect Park West, 5th Ave, Flatbush Ave) to document loose or dangling signs; interview DOT about maintenance schedules
Interview residents and business owners about near-misses or injuries; check if complaints cluster geographically

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 11 last week versus a baseline of 1.2 per week (780% spike, z-score 8.95), suggesting either a widespread public health issue or a failure in animal removal services THIS WEEK.
evidence: 11 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average over 8-week baseline
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Sanitation and Parks about dead animal removal response times and capacity; check for disease vectors (rats, raccoons, etc.)
Document specific locations of complaints; interview residents about health concerns or foul odors; investigate whether complaints are concentrated in one area (Prospect Park vs. streets)

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees and Branch Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 7 last week versus a 1.5 weekly baseline (367% increase, z-score 4.49), coinciding with spring season and suggesting poor Parks Department maintenance or liability risks from falling branches.
evidence: 7 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over 8-week baseline
367% spike with z-score of 4.49 (high statistical significance)
Aligns with community board's repeated budget request for park upgrades and reconstruction
reporting_angles: Check Parks Department trimming schedules; investigate whether budget constraints are delaying maintenance; document specific dangerous trees in Prospect Park or residential areas
Interview residents about near-misses with falling branches; photograph hazardous trees; compare complaint data across other districts to determine if this is localized

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping and Dirty Streets Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 26 (201% above baseline of 8.6, z-score 6.82), and dirty condition complaints reached 63 three weeks ago (211% above baseline of 20.2, z-score 4.91), suggesting a coordinated sanitation crisis or enforcement gap across the district.
evidence: 26 illegal dumping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 8.6 weekly baseline (201% spike, z-score 6.82)
63 dirty condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 20.2 weekly baseline (211% spike, z-score 4.91)
Converging signals suggest systemic sanitation failure affecting multiple complaint categories
reporting_angles: Map complaint clusters to identify hotspots (alleys, vacant lots, waterfront areas); interview Sanitation about collection schedules and enforcement actions; investigate whether gentrification or construction activity is driving dumping

Interview residents in high-complaint areas about quality-of-life impacts; investigate whether illegal dumping is organized (commercial waste) or opportunistic (residents); check if Gowanus Canal construction is exacerbating the issue

themes_detail.label: Homeless Services and Assistance Demand
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance requests spiked to 19 complaints 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 3.5 per week (443% increase, z-score 4.67), aligning with the community board's persistent budget requests for homelessness services and suggesting inadequate city resources.
evidence: 19 homeless person assistance complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.5 weekly baseline (443% spike, z-score 4.67)
Community board has repeatedly requested 'other services for the homeless' in annual budget cycles
High-severity classification suggests impact on resident safety and neighborhood livability
reporting_angles: Interview DHS about outreach capacity and housing availability; map complaint locations to identify encampment hotspots; investigate whether recent policy changes (shelter capacity limits, subway closures) are affecting Park Slope

Profile affected homeless individuals; interview residents and business owners about safety concerns; investigate whether gentrification is pushing houseless populations into the district; assess adequacy of drop-in centers and mental health services
